title: Tokenomics at scale: Track and cap Amazon Bedrock spend per IAM principal with CUR 2.0 and AWS Budgets
text: Generative AI spend is hard to attribute. Before an organization expands AI access, CFOs and CTOs usually want three answers: what do we spend per person or per team, can we cap it, and how much work does it take to get there. In our previous post, Tokenomics at Scale: How Jamf Built Real-Time Spend Enforcement for Amazon Bedrock, we explained a custom enforcement loop built on AWS IAM Identity Center, Amazon Athena over Amazon Bedrock model invocation logs, and AWS Lambda. This approach gives near-real-time control, but it requires code you then own and operate. This post shows how to get per-identity Amazon Bedrock cost visibility and enforceable spend limits using only AWS-native features, with no application code to write for the common case. The approach relies on three things: IAM principal attribution, which Amazon Bedrock records automatically; AWS Cost and Usage Reports (CUR) 2.0 or AWS Cost Explorer for reporting; and AWS Budgets with budget actions for enforcement. By the end, you will have per-identity cost reporting and an automatic guardrail that restricts Amazon Bedrock access when a threshold is crossed.
